query: Wang Yi China Foreign Minister visit South Korea 2026 postponed Taiwan dispute rescheduled July August 2026
answer:
I've completed my research on Wang Yi's postponed visit to South Korea. Here's the key summary:

**Current status (as of July 16, 2026):** Wang Yi's visit to South Korea — expected in Q1 2026 — remains **postponed and unscheduled**. There is **no confirmed rescheduled date for July or August 2026**. A ROK Foreign Ministry official said only that it "has now reached the stage of trying to coordinate a possible time."

**The Taiwan dispute (core cause):** After Taiwan complained about "China (Taiwan)" labeling on South Korea's electronic entry cards, Seoul removed the departure/destination fields on March 31, 2026. Beijing objected, with its MOFA asserting on April 14 that the "China (Taiwan)" label is "entirely natural" under the one-China principle. Korean media reported China put the visit on hold over this — though Seoul officially denied the connection, calling the change "a simple administrative and technical adjustment."

**Notable context:** Wang went to Pyongyang (April 8-10) instead, meeting Kim Jong Un; China reportedly also denied entry to South Korea's spy chief; and China-DPRK exchanges have accelerated (Wang Huning to Pyongyang July 15) while China-ROK ties have stalled.

**Important caveat:** No source confirms any specific rescheduled July/August 2026 date. The two governments frame the situation differently — Seoul downplays the Taiwan link, while Korean media and Beijing's signaling point to Taiwan as the friction point. Note also that the AskNews tools were unavailable (inactive subscription), so this relied on web search and direct article fetches.

key_facts: Wang Yi's planned visit to South Korea, expected in Q1 2026, was postponed and remains unscheduled as of mid-July 2026 with no confirmed dates for July or August 2026.
The dispute centers on 'China (Taiwan)' labeling on South Korea's electronic entry cards; Seoul removed the departure/destination fields on March 31, 2026 after Taiwan complained.
On April 14, 2026, China's MOFA spokesperson said Taiwan is part of China and calling it 'China (Taiwan)' is 'entirely natural,' signaling displeasure over Seoul's change.
South Korea's Foreign Ministry officially denied the labeling change caused the delay, calling it 'a simple administrative and technical adjustment' (statement April 20, 2026).
As of July 16, 2026, a ROK MOFA official said the visit 'has now reached the stage of trying to coordinate a possible time' — no finalized reschedule.
Wang Yi last visited South Korea in November 2023; he instead visited North Korea (Pyongyang) around April 8-10, 2026 and met Kim Jong Un.
The visit was intended as a follow-up to the January 2026 Lee Jae Myung-Xi Jinping summit and tied to diplomacy ahead of an anticipated Trump-Xi summit.
Around April 2026, China reportedly denied entry to South Korea's National Intelligence Service director amid the tensions.
China-DPRK high-level exchanges accelerated (Wang Huning visited Pyongyang from July 15, 2026), contrasting with stalled China-ROK exchanges.
